title: Thirty Straight: UConn Buries Illinois
dek: Tied 23-23 late in the first half, UConn scored the next 30 points against Illinois in Boston and rolled 77-52 into a second straight Final Four.

setup.text: A year after its fifth national title, UConn reached the Elite Eight at 34-3, the tournament's No. 1 overall seed and champion of both the Big East regular season and tournament. Its first three NCAA games were routs: 91-52 over Stetson, 75-58 over Northwestern and 82-52 over San Diego State, a rematch of the 2023 final.

TD Garden sits about 90 miles from Storrs, and the heavily pro-UConn crowd was one the Huskies called 'Storrs North.' Bill Murray, whose son Luke is a UConn assistant, watched from courtside, and Larry David sat in the first row.

Illinois, the region's No. 3 seed at 29-8 and the Big Ten tournament champion, had the most efficient offense in the country. Terrence Shannon Jr. had scored at least 25 in seven straight games, including 29 against Iowa State in the Sweet 16. The Illini had not been this deep in the tournament since 2005.

game.text: Donovan Clingan, the 7-foot-2 center from Connecticut, scored the game's first seven points, and Illinois did not score until after the first media timeout, trailing 9-0.
Then the game turned into a grind. UConn missed its first 10 3-point attempts and Tristen Newton went 0-for-6 in the half, while Marcus Domask kept Illinois close with 15 first-half points.

Illinois went scoreless again between the under-12 and under-8 timeouts, missing 11 shots in a row, and managed just four first-half points with Clingan on the floor. Still, back-to-back Domask baskets tied it 23-23 inside the final two minutes of the half.

sequence.text: Domask's jumper ties the game. It is Illinois' last basket for more than nine minutes of game clock.
Alex Karaban grabs an offensive rebound and kicks it to Hassan Diarra, who drains a 3. The run begins.
Newton, still without a field goal, makes two free throws. UConn leads 28-23 at the half.
Clingan scores on the Huskies' first possession of the second half.
Clingan dunks a Stephon Castle feed to finish a 7-0 start to the half. Illinois calls timeout.
Cam Spencer's jumper makes it 11-0 to open the half and the lead 16. Illinois calls timeout again.
Karaban's 3, from a Spencer pass, pushes the run to 21-0.
Clingan makes two free throws and goes to the bench with UConn up 23.
On the next Illinois trip, Clingan's replacement, Samson Johnson, blocks Shannon under the basket and finishes the fast break himself.
Karaban dunks a Newton pass, is fouled by Shannon and makes the free throw.

Spencer steals the ball and feeds Diarra for a layup: 30-0. Illinois has missed 16 shots in a row; one more miss will make it 17 straight, the last three of the first half and the first 14 of the second.
Justin Harmon finally scores for Illinois. UConn's lead is 28, on its way to 77-52.

quotes.text: It was a special level of basketball that we were playing.
We obviously came out in the second half and got blitzed.
It felt like no shots were going in. And it felt like they were getting out in transition and scoring every single time.
I didn't even realize we were on a 30-0 run in the moment, we were having so much fun out there.
quotes.when: as quoted by NCAA.com's Mike Lopresti, April 5, 2024

aftermath.text: UConn, which had played its first four NCAA games in Brooklyn and Boston, boarded a plane for the first time in almost a month to head to the Final Four outside Phoenix.
The Huskies were the first reigning champion to return to the Final Four since Florida in 2006-07, and it was the first time UConn had reached back-to-back Final Fours.
In Glendale, Ariz., UConn beat Alabama 86-72 and Purdue 75-60 to repeat as national champion.

legacy.text: NCAA.com's Mike Lopresti called the 30-0 run the number that best defined UConn's dominance that spring. Through four games UConn's combined margin was 111 points, the fourth-largest for any team heading into a Final Four, behind 1993 Kentucky, 1999 Duke and 1996 Kentucky, according to CBS Sports.
Two years later the teams met again in the 2026 Final Four in Indianapolis, and UConn won again, 71-62.

unsure: Whether 30-0 is the longest run in NCAA tournament history: ESPN said only that the onslaught was 'not seen this late in the NCAA tournament recently.' No record claim is made.
The TV crew comes from a pregame listing ('scheduled to be'); the replay's audio confirms booth voices addressed as Kevin and Dan, but Van Gundy's and Katz's roles were not independently confirmed.
AP calls Illinois' offense the most efficient in the country; CBS calls it the No. 2 offense. The narrative uses AP's wording.
